title: wmti walks itself
description: A guided tour of the wmti viewer's own architecture: a pure core wrapped in a thin Neovim shell. Read top to bottom to see how a single :Wmti turns a JSON file into a stepped, drift-tolerant tour.

steps.title: One command, many subcommands
steps.why: The plugin exposes a single :Wmti command that dispatches on its first argument (open is the default), with Tab-completion over the subcommand table. Native Vim command names must be uppercase + alphanumeric, so this is the idiomatic stand-in for a lowercase `wmti` / `wmti next` CLI feel — and it lets lazy.nvim defer loading until you actually run it.

steps.title: Open flow: notify, auto, or pick
steps.why: The open decision lives here, not in the UI: zero walkthroughs notify, exactly one auto-opens (no wasted keystroke), many fall through to the picker. :Wmti select reuses select() to always re-prompt.

steps.title: The filesystem boundary
steps.why: All disk access for walkthroughs is funneled through this module: glob .wmti/*.json, read bytes, hand the string to core.load. Keeping I/O here is what lets core stay pure and testable without touching a real file.

steps.title: The heart: drift-tolerant resolve
steps.why: This is why the viewer survives code moving after authoring. It matches the step's anchor text against the current buffer (exact, then whitespace-trimmed), picks the occurrence nearest the recorded line, and re-spans — falling back to the raw line with a 'moved' flag when the anchor is gone. Pure function, no Neovim.

steps.title: Jumping inside your own window
steps.why: goto_step is the seam between pure logic and the editor. It loads the step's file with nvim_win_set_buf (never :edit) so 'switchbuf' and autocmds can't fling the code into an extra window — the jump stays in your main window. A swap file can't crash it, it centers + highlights the resolved range, then hands focus back to the sidebar so stepping keeps flowing.

steps.title: Color coding the explanation
steps.why: The sidebar is a dumb projection of session state, re-rendered each step. These highlight groups give it structure at a glance — the title, the current step, file locations, status flags, and the why-prose each get their own color, all linked default=true so your colorscheme still wins.

steps.anchor: h.test("resolve relocates to the exact anchor when lines have drifted", function()
steps.title: Proof the drift handling works
steps.why: core is the single tested seam. This spec injects a lines table where the anchored code has shifted down and asserts resolve relocates to it — exercising the exact behavior step 4 promises, with zero Neovim, git, or real files involved.
